title: Launcher catalog schema omits the new inlined `bundle` summary object (tolerated, not read)
location: backend crates/catalog/src/dto.rs:54-73 (ClientDto.bundle: Option<BundleSummaryDto>) + dto.rs:22-30 (BundleSummaryDto{slug,version,status,filesCount,manifestUrl}); launcher src/shared/contracts/client.ts:15-44 (ClientResponseSchema)
detail: The refactor added an inlined `bundle` object to each client (slug/version/status/filesCount/manifestUrl). The launcher's ClientResponseSchema does not declare `bundle`, and Zod object parsing strips unknown keys by default, so the field is silently dropped. This is non-breaking because the launcher drives its bundle phase off the top-level `bundleSlug` (still served at dto.rs:65 and read in clientsApi.ts:61 via coerceBundleSlug) and fetches the manifest itself. But it means the new server-provided `manifestUrl`/`status`/`filesCount`/`version` are unused — if the launcher ever wants to skip a manifest round-trip or show bundle status/version, the data is already on the wire and just needs adding to the schema.
fix: Optionally extend ClientResponseSchema with an optional `bundle` object ({slug,version:nullable,status,filesCount,manifestUrl}) and surface it in normalizeClient, so the launcher can consume server-side bundle status/manifestUrl instead of re-deriving. No change needed if the current bundleSlug-only flow is intended.

title: Bundled yggdrasil-client carries authserver/sessionserver/bulkProfiles paths that would mis-resolve against the launcher's bare apiRoot — latent, never invoked
location: launcher src/main/services/auth/yggdrasilClient.ts:23-25 (apiRoot: mainConfig.apiUrl); node_modules/@loontail/yggdrasil-client client.ts:132-146 (bulkProfiles → '/api/profiles/minecraft'), 50-120 (authenticate/refresh/validate/invalidate → '/authserver/*'); backend crates/server/src/main.rs:112-116 (yggdrasil nested under /api/yggdrasil) + crates/yggdrasil/src/lib.rs:58-75
detail: The launcher constructs YggdrasilClient with apiRoot = bare apiUrl (correct for textures, which the backend serves top-level at /textures). But the same client's authenticate/refresh/validate/invalidate/profile/bulkProfiles/meta methods build URLs as apiRoot+endpoint (e.g. apiUrl + '/authserver/authenticate' or apiUrl + '/api/profiles/minecraft'). The backend only mounts those under /api/yggdrasil, so calling them through this bare-rooted client would 404. This is NOT a live break: a grep confirms the launcher only ever calls texturesClient for getTextures/uploadSkin/uploadCape/deleteSkin/deleteCape (all /textures/*); login/refresh go through the separate authApi.ts HTTP client, and in-game auth goes through authlib-injector pointed at yggdrasilApiRoot. The risk is purely future: any code that reaches for texturesClient.authenticate/bulkProfiles/profile would silently hit the wrong path.
fix: Either rename/narrow the launcher type to expose only the texture methods (it already only surfaces texturesClient+fetchTextures), or add a code comment that this instance is textures-only and the non-texture methods must not be used with the bare apiRoot. No functional change required today.

title: Stale comments reference the retired CMS/Strapi `publicUrl`/`server.url` plugin contract
location: launcher src/main/services/bundle/api.ts:24-26 ("when the plugin's publicUrl is unset and server.url is empty") and :17-18 ("the CMS serializes consistently"); src/main/services/bundle/manager.ts and verify.ts:18 still say "CMS"/"plugin"
detail: Several comments still describe the old Strapi-plugin behavior (publicUrl/server.url fallback, CMS serialization) that no longer exists — the backend now serves artifacts.json verbatim from disk (crates/bundles/src/public.rs:18-50) with url fields fixed at /bundle-registry/builds/{slug}/files/{path} (crates/bundles/src/storage.rs:52-56, manifest.rs). The behavior the comments rely on (server may emit root-relative URLs → launcher absolutizes against apiUrl) still happens to hold because the backend's url fields are always server-relative and api.ts:91 absolutizes them, so functionality is correct; only the rationale text is outdated.
fix: Update the comments in bundle/api.ts (and the 'CMS'/'plugin' wording in manager.ts/verify.ts) to describe the native Rust bundle-registry contract instead of the retired Strapi plugin. Pure doc cleanup.

title: Dead renderer registration slice: useRegister hook + register api never called by any UI
detail: useRegister (hooks.ts:87) is a fully-built React-Query mutation hook with no consumer. Proof: `grep -rn useRegister src tests` returns only the definition line. Its only feeder, the `register` api function (api.ts:7), is referenced solely by `registerWithRejectionResult` (hooks.ts:38) which is referenced solely by the dead useRegister. LoginForm.tsx (the only auth UI) imports only useLogin and useMojangLogin — there is no signup form. The whole renderer-side registration vertical (useRegister -> register -> auth.register invoke) is unreachable. The main-side handler registerAuthRoutes/auth.register and RegisterPayload schema are still live/constrained by the contract coverage test, so this is a half-wired feature.
fix: Remove useRegister (hooks.ts:87-109), the register api fn (api.ts:7-8), and registerWithRejectionResult (hooks.ts:38-44); drop `register` from the api import in hooks.ts:16 and the now-unused RegisterPayload import. Decide separately whether to also retire the main-side auth.register handler + IpcContract entry (would require updating contractCoverage.test.ts and channels.ts) or keep it for a future signup UI.
area: Dead-code audit of loontail-launcher/src (Electron main/renderer/preload/shared)

title: Dead renderer build-edit slice: useUpdateBuild hook + updateBuild api never consumed

By contrast useCreateBuild and useDeleteBuild ARE used in components (CreateBuildModal.tsx, BuildSettingsTab.tsx). There is no edit-build modal, so the 'update build' feature is dead on the renderer. Main-side builds.update handler (instances/routes.ts:29) and UpdateInstancePayload remain live/constrained by the coverage test.
fix: Remove useUpdateBuild (hooks.ts:62), drop it from the catalog/index.ts barrel re-export (index.ts:9), and remove the updateBuild api fn (api.ts:18-19). Decide separately about retiring the main-side builds.update channel/handler.

location: src/shared/contracts/auth.ts:73 MojangProfile, :82 YggdrasilProfile; bundle.ts:79 LocalManifestFile; client.ts:10 Keyword; instance.ts:23 InstanceBundleRef, :36 InstancePresentation, :45 InstanceLoader, :54 InstanceOrigin; settings.ts:32 StorageSettings; updater.ts:9 UpdaterState; constants/errorCodes.ts:9 ErrorCode

title: Bundle SyncTask carries dead 'compat' getter/setter views over phase, plus a parallel result shape, both gated by stale W5-T5 TODOs
detail: SyncTask has a real `phase: 'running'|'paused'|'cancelled'` field, but ALSO exposes `paused`/`cancelled` as getter/setter pairs that translate to/from `phase` via markPaused/markCancelled/markRunning. runner.ts comments call these 'Backward-compatible views over phase ... Kept until W5-T5 collapses the manager catch-decode'. Separately, runSyncPhases returns SyncPhasesResult={outcome, deletedAny, paused, cancelled} where paused/cancelled are just `outcome==='paused'`/`'==='cancelled'` (syncPhasesResult helper, runner.ts:72-80) — a second redundant view, also justified only by the W5-T5 note. The manager's resolved path already reads `result.outcome` (manager.ts:364) while the catch path still reads `task.cancelled`/`task.paused` (manager.ts:391-407). The whole 'compat view' scaffolding is transitional code that was never removed.
fix: Collapse to one representation. Make workers/manager read `task.phase` directly (e.g. `task.phase==='cancelled'`) and drop the paused/cancelled accessor pair from SyncTask; replace mutations with `task.phase = ...` guarded by the existing mark* helpers. Drop the `paused`/`cancelled` fields from SyncPhasesResult and have manager.ts:364 keep using `result.outcome`. Net deletion of ~30 lines of accessors + 2 derived fields with no behavior change (the transition guards stay in mark*).

title: OpRegistry is a Map wrapper that re-exposes its backing Map (.map); consumers mutate it directly, so the class adds nothing
detail: OpRegistry wraps a `Map<CatalogKey,Op>` and forwards get/set/delete/has/keys 1:1. Its own comment admits the backing Map is shared into ManagerEnv.ops via `.map` and 'mutated by the consumer modules through that reference'. So install/launch/repair/uninstall mutate the raw Map while the manager calls the wrapper — two access paths to the same Map. The wrapper provides no invariant, encapsulation, or added behavior.
fix: Delete OpRegistry and the `.map` getter; use `Map<CatalogKey,Op>` directly in MinecraftManager and pass that Map as `env.ops`. The constructor's `ops: OpRegistry = new OpRegistry()` becomes `ops = new Map()`. Replace `ops.set/get/delete/has/keys` calls (already Map-compatible) verbatim. Replace the test-only `seedOp(registry,key,op)` with `map.set(key,op)`.

title: SyncStateStore is a no-value Map wrapper

BundleManager already takes it as an injectable (`activeSyncs: SyncStateStore = new SyncStateStore()`), but a plain Map is equally injectable and has the same API surface the manager uses.

title: Three independent rolling byte-speed window implementations
detail: The same 'sample [ms,bytes], prune to window, reset on backwards jump, rate=(last-first)/dt' logic is reimplemented three times with the same 4s/1s window semantics and the same 'don't go negative on resume' comment. progressAdapter and useByteSpeed are nearly line-for-line identical (both even document the identical 4s window rationale).
fix: Extract one pure helper (e.g. shared `createSpeedWindow(windowMs)` returning {push(bytes):number, reset()}) and have all three call sites use it. The renderer hook wraps it in useEffect; the two main-process samplers call push() per chunk/snapshot. Removes ~2 copies of the sampling/pruning loop.

title: Atomic JSON-write (mkdir + tmp write + rm + rename + tmp cleanup) duplicated; atomicReplace exists but is wrapped redundantly
detail: atomicReplace already encapsulates the rm-dest + rename + tmp-cleanup. saveLocalManifest re-implements the 'mkdir, write tmp, on-error rm tmp' wrapper around it; saveInstanceManifest re-implements the ENTIRE dance inline (mkdir + writeFile tmp + rm target + rename + catch rm tmp) and does NOT even call atomicReplace, despite a comment claiming it 'matches the bundle/install manifest writers'. Three loadManifest readers (manifestRepo, instanceRepo, plus installManifest) also share an identical readFile→JSON.parse→safeParse→ENOENT-null pattern.
fix: Add `writeJsonAtomic(target, value)` (mkdir dirname, write `${target}.tmp`, atomicReplace) and `readJsonValidated(target, schema)` in infra, and route saveLocalManifest/saveInstanceManifest/installManifest through them. Deletes the inline duplicate in instanceRepo and the wrapper boilerplate in manifestRepo.

title: db/repos: seedAuthRow and writeAuthRow are byte-identical
detail: writeAuthRow(db, metadata, secret: Buffer) and seedAuthRow(db, metadata, secret: Buffer|null) execute the exact same INSERT...ON CONFLICT statement. The only difference is the parameter type (Buffer vs Buffer|null); the SQL and runtime behavior are identical. The comment justifies seedAuthRow by tolerance of a null secret, but writeAuthRow would accept null at runtime too.
fix: Delete seedAuthRow and widen writeAuthRow's signature to `secret: Buffer | null`. Update the one legacyImport caller. Net -8 lines.

title: Two near-identical renderer event-listener components + zustand stores + status seeders + broadcasters (bundle vs minecraft)
location: src/renderer/features/minecraft/events.ts:73-107 & bundle/events.ts:10-45; minecraft/store.ts & bundle/store.ts; bundle/statusSeeder.ts vs minecraft/hooks.ts:13; main/services/minecraft/broadcast.ts & bundle/broadcast.ts
detail: The minecraft and bundle stacks repeat the same shapes: (a) a useEffect listener that subscribes to status/progress/error, patches a zustand store, toasts errors; (b) a zustand store with `entries: Record<slug,State>`, a `patch` that merges + clears progress/error on terminal statuses, and a `selectX(slug)` selector; (c) a createStatusSeeder instance; (d) a createBroadcaster with status/progress/error each calling `emit(getWindow(), CHANNEL, payload)`. The store patch/clear-set logic differs only in which status sets clear which fields.
fix: These are partial dups — don't force a single generic if it obscures the field-clearing tables. Highest-value, lowest-risk wins: (1) factor the createBroadcaster trio into `makeBroadcaster(getWindow, {status,progress,error}channels)` (both are mechanically identical); (2) factor the store into a shared `createRuntimeStore({default, terminalStatuses, clearErrorStatuses, clearProgressFields})` factory. Leave the two event listeners separate (their side-effects/invalidations genuinely diverge).

title: useSlugMutation + mutationMeta pattern duplicated verbatim across minecraft and bundle hooks

title: MinecraftManager repeats the 'register BUNDLE_SYNCING op, run hook, drop op' block three times
detail: Three sites build `const bundleOp = {kind:BUNDLE_SYNCING, abort:new AbortController()}`, set it, await `hook(slug, bundleOp.abort.signal)`, catch with an 'aborted → not an error' guard, and `finally ops.delete(slug)`. The bodies differ only in the surrounding status emit on failure and the log level. The repeated comment 'Register a BUNDLE_SYNCING op ... symmetric with startLaunch' confirms the intent to share.
fix: Extract `private async runBundleSyncPhase(slug, hook, opts:{onFailure?})`: claims the BUNDLE_SYNCING op, awaits hook, applies the shared abort/log/cleanup, lets callers pass the failure status emit. Collapses ~60 lines to ~25 and centralizes the abort-vs-error decoding.

title: BundleManager.tryGetClient and fetchClient differ only in error handling; getInstallState/runSync each re-derive folder/bundleSlug

title: Pausing a launch-triggered bundle sync freezes the Play flow until the 5-minute idle timeout
detail: runSync creates a forLaunch awaiter (createAwaiter) and does `await launchWait` after executePreparedSync. The awaiter only settles via resolveAwaiters (COMPLETED) / rejectAwaiters (ERROR or cancel). When pauseSync is invoked on a forLaunch sync, the runner throws ABORTED, executePreparedSync's catch sees `ABORTED && task.paused` and returns WITHOUT resolving/rejecting the awaiter, and its finally does not drop the active sync (task.paused true). So `await launchWait` in runSync never settles. MinecraftManager.startLaunch is blocked inside `await launchHook(...)`, the BUNDLE_SYNCING op stays set, and the client is stuck on LAUNCHING. It only unblocks after BUNDLE_PAUSED_SYNC_MAX_IDLE_MS (5 min, constants/bundle.ts:21) when expirePausedSync rejects the awaiter with ABORTED. The bundlePause IPC route (bundle/routes.ts:14-17) is not gated on forLaunch, so the user can trigger this. Net effect: pause during a Play-time sync freezes the Play button for up to 5 minutes (or until the user separately cancels).
fix: Disallow pause for forLaunch syncs (pauseSync: `if (active.forLaunch) return;` or treat pause as cancel during launch), OR make the forLaunch awaiter reject immediately when a forLaunch sync is paused (e.g. in pauseSync, if active.forLaunch call rejectAwaiters with ABORTED before parking, or convert forLaunch pause into cancelSync). Simplest: in pauseSync, `if (active.forLaunch) { this.cancelSync(slug); return; }`.
area: launcher main process (Electron): bundle sync/download, minecraft install/launch, sqlite store, auth/session, IPC

title: Concurrent/duplicate session refreshes are not de-duplicated; can clobber a freshly rotated session and waste single-use rotations
detail: Session rotation is single-use server-side ('the old token is revoked server-side' — authApi.ts:69-70). httpRequest fires port.refresh() on any 401/403 with no in-flight de-dup. The launcher issues many session-auth requests in parallel (catalog, bundle manifest fetch via fetchRemoteManifest with auth:'session', media cache). If several land while the token is stale, each independently calls refresh() with the SAME old token; the first rotates it, the rest POST /auth/refresh with the now-revoked token and get `expired`, returning null — so their retries fail even though a valid token now exists. Worse, verify.ts:verifySession also calls loontailAuth.refresh concurrently and does setStoredAuth on its own result; a refresh racing with a login's setStoredAuth (auth.ts:completeAuthentication) can overwrite the new session with a stale-derived one. There is no mutex around refresh/setStoredAuth.
fix: Memoize the in-flight refresh in http.ts (and/or buildSessionAuthPort): keep a `let refreshing: Promise<string|null> | null`; on refresh, if one is in flight return it, else start it and clear in finally. Also re-read the current token before refreshing and, if it already changed since the request's token, retry with the new token instead of refreshing again. Consider a single shared refresh path used by both http.ts and verifySession.
area: launcher main process (Electron): bundle sync/download, minecraft install/launch, sqlite store, auth/session, IPC

title: getStoredAuth destroys the stored session on a transient secure-storage/decrypt failure
detail: getStoredAuth is a read used on the launch path (launch.ts:312 resolveLaunchAuth(account, getStoredAuth())) and elsewhere. On any throw from decryptAuthSecret/hydrateSession/validation it calls clearStoredAuth() — a destructive delete of the auth row. decryptAuthSecret throws not only for corrupt blobs but also when safeStorage is transiently unavailable (assertSecureStorageAvailable: e.g. Linux keyring/DBus not yet ready, or 'Secure auth storage is unavailable'). A transient secure-storage hiccup therefore permanently drops a still-valid session and forces a full re-login, instead of failing soft (return null, keep the row for the next attempt). The migrateLegacyAuthSession path (clearStoredAuth on failure) has the same shape.
fix: Distinguish 'storage unavailable' (transient → return null without deleting) from 'blob present but corrupt/invalid' (delete). E.g. only clearStoredAuth() when the blob exists and fails schema validation, not when safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable() is false. Have assertSecureStorageAvailable throw a tagged error that getStoredAuth treats as non-destructive.
area: launcher main process (Electron): bundle sync/download, minecraft install/launch, sqlite store, auth/session, IPC

title: Windows path case-sensitivity gap can mark remote-owned bundle files for deletion (and heal-thrash)
location: src/main/services/bundle/paths.ts:46-47 (normalizePathForSet only swaps backslashes, no case fold) + services/bundle/plan.ts:104-147 (bundleOwnedRelativePaths / toDelete) + manifestSnapshot.ts flattenRemote
detail: normalizePathForSet only converts `\`→`/`; it does not case-fold. bundleOwnedRelativePaths is built from the current remote manifest's paths, and toDelete is `local.files` keys not present in that set. On Windows the filesystem is case-insensitive, so if the remote manifest ever emits a path with different casing than what a prior local manifest recorded (e.g. remote 'Mods/x.jar' vs local 'mods/x.jar'), `bundleOwnedRelativePaths.has(localPath)` returns false and the still-owned file is queued for deletion in runDeletePhase, then the heal pass churns. Same normalization feeds classifyEntry's `local?.files[normalizedKey]` skip fast-path, so a casing drift also forces needless re-downloads. resolveSafeEntryPath resolves to the real (possibly differently-cased) disk path regardless, so the delete can actually remove a wanted file.
fix: On Windows (or unconditionally, if the CMS guarantees stable casing is not assumable), case-fold keys used purely for set membership and local-manifest lookup: e.g. `normalizePathForSet(p) = p.replace(/\\/g,'/')` plus a separate `toComparisonKey(p)` that also lowercases, and build bundleOwnedRelativePaths / local.files lookups against the comparison key. Keep the original-cased path for the actual fs operation.
area: launcher main process (Electron): bundle sync/download, minecraft install/launch, sqlite store, auth/session, IPC

title: Cancel landing after heal completes but before the final pause-check emits COMPLETED instead of CANCELLED
detail: After runSyncPhases returns 'completed' and the deletedAny heal runs to success, the only guard before completePreparedSync(COMPLETED) is `if (task.paused) return;`. A cancelSync arriving in that window sets task.cancelled (not paused), so the code proceeds to emit COMPLETED and resolve forLaunch awaiters, rather than CANCELLED. The heal call itself throws ABORTED if cancelled mid-heal (healer.ts:122-125), so the window is narrow (cancel strictly between heal resolving and the check), and the actual work is already done, so it is mostly cosmetic — but a forLaunch cancel would then resolve (launch proceeds) instead of rejecting.
fix: Make the post-heal guard also honor cancel: `if (task.cancelled) throw new BundleError(ABORTED, 'cancelled after heal'); if (task.paused) return;` so the catch emits CANCELLED and rejects awaiters consistently.
area: launcher main process (Electron): bundle sync/download, minecraft install/launch, sqlite store, auth/session, IPC

title: downloadEntry hash-mismatch on the finish path leaks the stale .tmp on the success-shaped reject
location: src/main/services/bundle/download.ts:169-186 (writeStream 'finish' handler hash check) vs 195-210 (.catch tmp cleanup)
detail: On a SHA-256 mismatch the finish handler sets settled=true, calls cleanup(), then `reject(...)` for the integrity error. That reject is caught by the outer `.catch` (line 195) which does remove the tmp — so cleanup of the tmp does happen. However, the integrity reject does NOT call response.destroy()/writeStream.destroy() (unlike fail()); both are already finished so handles are closed, so this is benign. The genuinely fragile part: the integrity-failure BundleError is created with DOWNLOAD_INTEGRITY_FAILED, but the outer catch rethrows `if (err instanceof BundleError) throw err;` — correct. Net: behavior is correct today, but the finish-path reject bypasses the shared fail() helper, so a future change (e.g. needing stream teardown or settled accounting) can silently regress. Low-impact maintainability/robustness risk rather than an active bug.
fix: Route the hash-mismatch through the same fail() helper (or at minimum reuse its teardown), e.g. `return fail(new BundleError(DOWNLOAD_INTEGRITY_FAILED, ...))` after digesting, so all reject paths share settled/cleanup/teardown semantics.
area: launcher main process (Electron): bundle sync/download, minecraft install/launch, sqlite store, auth/session, IPC

title: cancelAll bundle drain can resolve before slow syncs finish their finally (tmp cleanup / manifest write) on quit
detail: On before-quit, drain() calls clientOperationLocks.cancelAll() then disposes services (bundleService.dispose → manager.cancelAll(250)). cancelAll races settled vs a 250ms timeout, so if a sync's finally (tmp rm, saveLocalManifest) is still running at 250ms, drain proceeds and index.ts calls closeDatabase(). A late saveLocalManifest is fs-only (no DB), so DB-close is safe; but a late persist that touched the store (none here for bundle) could hit a closed DB. The actual risk is a partially-written local manifest .tmp left behind if the process exits during the rename window — acceptable per the documented best-effort cleanup, but worth noting the 250ms bound can truncate legitimate cleanup on slow disks/AV.
fix: Either raise/await the bundle drain unconditionally during shutdown (it already uses unref timers so it won't block exit forever), or ensure no store/DB writes occur in the post-timeout window. Current behavior is defensible; document that DB writes must never run in a sync's finally.
area: launcher main process (Electron): bundle sync/download, minecraft install/launch, sqlite store, auth/session, IPC

title: WAL database closed without checkpoint on quit; last writes may sit only in -wal until next open
detail: journal_mode=WAL is enabled but closeDatabase just calls instance.close() with no explicit `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`. better-sqlite3's close does finalize and SQLite checkpoints on the last connection close in most cases, so this is usually fine; however, if the process is force-terminated during drain (the before-quit drain is async and app.quit() is only called after it settles, but window-all-closed / OS kill can preempt), recent writes live in the -wal file. They are recovered on next open, so this is durability-on-clean-exit only, not corruption. Calling it out because last-played / settings writes are synchronous and expected to persist immediately.
fix: Optionally run `db.pragma('wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)')` before close, or set `db.pragma('journal_mode = WAL'); db.pragma('synchronous = NORMAL')` is already implied — add a checkpoint in closeDatabase for a clean shutdown. Low priority since WAL recovers on next open.
area: launcher main process (Electron): bundle sync/download, minecraft install/launch, sqlite store, auth/session, IPC

title: cache media protocol is an SSRF and session-bearer exfiltration primitive
detail: The renderer wraps any http/https media URL (from CMS/catalog or texture lookups) into a cache scheme URL via toCachedMediaUrl and renders it in an img tag. The main-process cache protocol handler decodes it, checks only that the scheme is http/https, then calls fetch with sessionAuthHeader(). sessionAuthHeader (infra/http.ts:117-120) attaches the API session Bearer UNCONDITIONALLY with no check that the host is mainConfig.apiUrl. So a media URL is enough to (1) make the main process fetch arbitrary internal hosts like 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254 (SSRF the renderer/CSP cannot reach), and (2) leak the user API bearer to an attacker host. URLs are attacker-influenceable via any CMS media field (officialSource/catalog contracts pass MediaRef.url verbatim) and fully controllable by a compromised renderer. The bundle downloader pins host scheme + redirect origin in urlPolicy.ts; the media path has no equivalent.
fix: Host-allowlist the decoded URL to mainConfig.apiUrl origin (plus any explicit public CDN) and reject others. Only attach sessionAuthHeader when the host is the trusted API origin. Use redirect:'manual' and re-validate Location origin so a 30x cannot smuggle the bearer cross-host.
area: Electron launcher security audit

title: Session API bearer passed to the game JVM as a -D system property, readable via local process listing
detail: buildNetworkAgentJvmArgs appends a JVM system property carrying the universal API bearer (getStoredSessionToken) to the Java command line. Full command lines are readable by any same-user process on Windows/macOS/Linux (Task Manager command-line column, WMIC, Get-CimInstance Win32_Process, ps -ww, /proc/pid/cmdline), so any local process can read the live bearer that authenticates catalogue/bundle/textures/network as the user. The composed command is also written to disk via the launch info log at launch.ts:364.
fix: Pass the token out of band: a process env var (not logged, narrower than argv) or a 0600 file / stdin handshake / localhost loopback the agent reads once. At minimum redact the serviceToken from the launch command log line.
area: Electron launcher security audit

title: Bundle manifest entry hosts not pinned to the API origin; bearer attached to whatever host the manifest names
detail: The downloader attaches sessionAuthHeader. resolveBundleRedirectUrl correctly blocks HTTPS->HTTP downgrade and pins each redirect hop to the initial origin. The gap: the INITIAL entry URL is only scheme-validated, not host-validated. assertAllowedBundleAssetUrl accepts any https host and resolveBundleManifestEntryUrl does not require the result to stay on the API host, so a compromised/misconfigured CMS manifest can point a file at an arbitrary https host and the launcher fetches it with the bearer attached. Same class as SSRF-1 but gated behind manifest control.
fix: Require the asset host to equal the API origin (or an explicit asset-CDN allowlist) in resolveBundleManifestEntryUrl/validateBundleAssetDownloadUrl. Only attach sessionAuthHeader when the request host is the trusted API origin.
area: Electron launcher security audit

title: Renderer CSP allows img-src https for any host (image-beacon exfil channel)
detail: Scripts are well scoped (script-src self, no unsafe-inline/eval) and connect-src is self + apiOrigin only. But img-src is 'self data blob https cache' — open https lets the renderer load images from any HTTPS host, giving an XSS/renderer foothold a classic data-exfil channel via image URLs. style-src 'unsafe-inline' is a documented react-aria trade-off.
fix: Restrict img-src to self/data/blob/cache plus explicit API+CDN origins instead of open https, routing remote images through the hardened cache proxy. Keep style-src unsafe-inline only while react-aria needs it.
area: Electron launcher security audit

title: Console window runs with sandbox disabled
detail: The console BrowserWindow sets sandbox:false (documented workaround for dropped contextBridge push batches in backgrounded sandboxed windows). contextIsolation/nodeIntegration are correct and the trusted-sender check restricts the console to an explicit channel allowlist (cannot invoke auth/launch/settings/system). Residual risk: a renderer RCE has a larger blast radius unsandboxed; the console renders attacker-influenceable Minecraft stdout/stderr, so DOM-injection hygiene matters.
fix: Prefer sandbox:true with a pull model (console streams via ipcRenderer.invoke) or webContents.send which is not subject to the batching issue. If sandbox:false stays, keep the allowlist tight and render all console output as text (never dangerouslySetInnerHTML / unsanitized markdown).
area: Electron launcher security audit

title: Positive: core defenses verified (recorded to prevent regression)
location: src/main/windows/mainWindow.ts:46-72; secureWindow.ts:31-47; src/preload/index.ts:31-50; src/main/ipc/router.ts:61-96; src/main/infra/store.ts:200-403; src/main/services/bundle/paths.ts:15-37; electron-builder.yml:42-48
detail: No action required. Main window: sandbox/contextIsolation on, nodeIntegration off, webSecurity on, insecure content off; will-navigate and will-attach-webview blocked; window-open denied and openExternal HTTPS-host-allowlisted. Preload exposes only invoke/on/platform, no raw ipcRenderer. Router enforces trusted-sender + zod arg validation; console restricted to its channel allowlist. Permission handlers deny by default. Secrets only in safeStorage (versioned, Linux backend allowlist); legacy plaintext sessions purged/migrated. Path traversal blocked via resolveSafeEntryPath (download + delete); downloads verify SHA-256. Electron fuses fully set (runAsNode off, cookie encryption, ASAR integrity, onlyLoadAppFromAsar, NODE_OPTIONS/inspect off). DevTools auto-open dev-only. openPath restricted to launcher-owned canonical roots; Microsoft authorize URL host+path allowlisted.
fix: No change needed; treat as invariants in future review of window creation, preload, IPC, and secret store.
area: Electron launcher security audit
